field_values.redo_desc_about: Learn the history of the islands of the Hawkesbury – Lion Island, Dangar Island, Spectacle Island, Long Island, Peat Island, Milson Island, and Bar Island. Cruise past the water-access-only settlements of the Lower Hawkesbury, and see the wreck of the HMAS Parramatta, Australia's first warship, and find out how it ended up on the Hawkesbury River lying at the foot of spectacular sandstone cliffs.
field_values.redo_desc_requirements: This cruise requires a minimum of 25 people to run.
field_values.redo_booking_inclusions:
Morning tea served on arrival, with percolated coffee, hot tea, and delicious home-made ANZAC biscuits - we would bet you haven't had them like this before!
Lunch is served around midday, and consists of a very Aussie Ploughman's-style plate with a selection of cold meats (ham, beef, salami), tasty cheese, tomato, cucumber, carrot, mixed lettuce leaves, pickled onions, fresh Turkish Bread roll, pickles, fruit chutney, butter & Italian dressing.
We can cater for the common dietary requirements (gluten free, vegetarian etc) - just let us know at the time of booking.
All our boats are fully licensed, so you can enjoy a glass of wine or beer, or a soft drink, with your lunch. Water is always available at the bar.

field_values.redo_desc_about: Our Paddle & Picnic allows you to leave the world behind for a day of great water activities. The self-catered option is a 4 hour event for $75 per person and includes kayak hire, picnic set up and eskies with ice. You will arrive at our wharf location and we will start with a paddle and safety briefing. We will then get everyone into the kayaks to paddle to the beach where your picnic is set up. This is about a 30 minute paddle. You will then have about 3 hours there, followed by another 30 minute paddle back. While you paddle we will transfer any food, drinks or equipment over to the beach. Great for small and large groups you can make the day your own with a range of add-ons including, stand up paddleboarding, food and drink packages, beach yoga and more! Beach Picnics are able to be run 7 days a week. They require a minimum of six participants and we can cater for up to 110 people at one time.

GO Surf School runs SurfGrom programs in Port Fairy and Warrnambool over the summer months.

SurfGroms is a fun-filled, learn-to-surf program that teaches kids the essentials of ocean awareness and safe surfing. We love our beach culture and these are essential lifelong skills for every child growing up around the beaches in Victoria.

We have had a fantastic response to the SurfGrom program. Since its launch, thousands of children have experienced the thrill of surfing in Australia for the first time through SurfGroms. 

There are three achievement levels so kids can keep coming back and have fun learning the skills that will give them the confidence to become a surfer for life. as well as fundamental Ocean Awareness and Beach Safety skills such as surf survival and varying surf conditions at the beach.

Make a day of it and experience the real Australian outback! After seeing Uluru, Kata Tjuta, Lake Amadeus and Kings Canyon by air, land at Kings Creek Station, an authentic country airstrip, and choose one of the following adventures;

**Kings Creek Station Tour:**
Journey through magnificent desert oaks, cruise over rolling red sand dunes, and take in the vast views and roaming wildlife while learning all about outback life on a station in Central Australia.

**Karrke Cultural Experience:**
Immerse yourself in a truly authentic Aboriginal cultural experience. See, feel and experience Aboriginal culture up close.

**Kings Canyon Creek Bed Walk:**
Enjoy a drive along the George Gill Range to Kings Canyon for the Creek Bed Walk.

*A full-day tour taking in many of Dunedin's iconic buildings, landmarks and scenic lookouts. Included is a fully guided tour of New Zealand's infamous Castle built over a century ago by William Larnach high up on the hills of the Otago Peninsula.*
*Lunch is own cost, choose from a la carte to cafe style menu along with a variety of wine and beer selections
field_values.redo_desc_highlights:
Begin with day with a city sights tour visiting Baldwin Street. Time to have a walk on this world record-breaking street and marvel at the houses and people who live on it's steep gradient.
Drive through the University of Otago with its neo-gothic clock tower and quirky student accommodations. We will visit Dunedin's Octagon (city center) for a look at the Robbie Burns statue with St Paul's Cathedral and Town Hall in the background. We visit Dunedin's Grand Railway Station for a look at the wonderfully restored Flemish renaissance interior.
Then we are off to the Otago Peninsula for breath-taking views along the High road with photo stops as we travel on-route to Larnach Castle.
After lunch our guide will escort you throughout the entire castle, from the gun room below to the views from the turret and all the marvels in between. Rest assured your tour of the castle will be memorable and informative with many original artifacts on show. Enjoy our personal attention to detail as we explore the Larnach family’s legacy and tell of their amazing story.
The Castle's spectacular garden is one of national significance and there will be an opportunity to explore after the tour of the Castle.
field_values.redo_desc_what_included:
- Includes entry fees to the Castle and grounds and our very own guided tour inside.
- *Chilled NZ spring water provided for anyone who brings their own water bottle (we no longer provide bottled water to help reduce our waste footprint :+)

Our Warrnambool Wanderer Tour takes you past main attractions including the Botanical Gardens, Warrnambool Race Course – home to The Grand Annual Steeplechase and famous May Race Carnival. field_values.redo_desc_about:
This tour is truly Mother Nature at her best – with spectacular waves, rugged cliffs and rock formations. But it’s the rich history that makes the Shipwreck Coast such a fascinating place.
Drive through the countryside and past dairy farms while we make our way via the popular coastal town of Port Campbell to the iconic London Arch (which was London Bridge before it’s collapse in 1990). The Shipwreck Coast Tour also features The Grotto, Bay of Martyrs, Bay of Islands and one of the Great Ocean Road’s best kept secrets Childers Cove – the perfect location to escape the crowds but not the spectacular coastline. Here you can walk to the cove where you are surrounded by limestone cliffs.
You can also take a walk along the beach and marvel at the beauty of the location. Returning back to Warrnambool in time for lunch, a spot of shopping or explore Warrnambool’s Street Art Trail.

field_values.redo_desc_about: Get on board a Stand-Up Paddle Board! Learn the basics and experience the thrill of this growing water sport in the unique estuary environments of Byron OR the Tweed. Our waterways are teeming with marine and bird life - and adventure - in these lesser-explored, abundant natural worlds. We meet on site: Brunswick Heads - Exact location at Brunswick River and time TBC by instructor, according to tidal conditions; Pottsville - Hardy Park at Mooball Creek. All equipment is provided then you're ready to paddle! We start by taking you through the basics of Stand Up Paddle Boarding including stroke technique, balancing, turning and safety before we start the tour where your SUP adventure begins! Our professional and fun instructors stay with you on the water, guiding and gliding you through various features of the estuary, giving helpful tips along the way to improve your skills, technique and overall experience as we complete the 2-hour tour. We return to our original launch site invigorated, happy and .. ready for a drink or bite! In Brunswick Heads, try the iconic 'Brunz Hotel' in the heart of the village or in Pottsville, join the locals for 'a pot' or two at the nearby 'Potty Tavern.'

field_values.redo_desc_about: #Intimate guided walk through Puketi Forest, the ancient kauri rainforest (15,000 hectares) close to the Bay Islands. With over 360 indigenous species of plants, this subtropical rainforest is one of the most diverse in New Zealand. Learn to recognise and name some of the native trees: the mighty kauri, tawa, rimu, totara and nikau (New Zealand’s native palm tree) to mention just a few. Listen and maybe see the native birds: tui, fantail, pied tit, fernbird and kukupa. Spot the Northland green gecko and tusked weta. Experienced guides with a passion for conservation share their stories and knowledge: Learn more about the unique flora and fauna. Discover what’s threatening New Zealand’s subtropical rainforests: possums, stoats, ferrets and kauri dieback and what we can do to protect the eco system.

field_values.redo_desc_about: Waimangu Round Trip starts in the Waimangu Valley and ends at Te Wairoa - The Buried Village at Lake Tarawera. The customer starts their Journey at the Waimangu Volcanic Valley administration office and travels down the Waimangu Valley and boards the boat to cross Lake Rotomahana to the Rotomahana jetty to meet the guide from Totally Tarawera and walks across the Rotomahana Isthmus to the Te Ariki Jetty. Guests board the boat Sophia and is hosted on board by decendents of Tuhourangi. The boat then travels across Lake Tarawera while hearing the stories of the Tuhourangi guides that hosted international visitors to the Pink & White Terraces before the eruption of Tarawera in 1886. The boat travels past Te Rata Bay and Hot Water Beach on route to Punaromia -The Landing, Lake Tarawera. Guests then disembark the boat and board the bus to take the 5 minute journey to Te Wairoa - The Buried Village.

field_values.redo_desc_about: All aboard for a pleasant evening's journey from Mt Barker to Strathalbyn while celebrating Christmas in July with a difference. The journey commences from Mount Barker station - a pleasant 20 minute drive from Adelaide along the South Eastern Freeway. Your ticket includes a twilight three-course dinner at a Strathalbyn hotel and return travel from Mt Barker. Leaving Mt Barker late afternoon, listen to our heritage steam locomotive, as it hauls the train up to the crest of the line at Philcox Hill and then winds down the eastern escarpment of the southern Mt Lofty Ranges, passing through several long abandoned station sites which bear testimony to the importance of this branch line a century ago. Crossing the Angas River you then enter the historic township of Strathalbyn where many Scottish migrants settled in the early 1800s, influencing the early architecture which is still evident today. The town is well worth a return visit during the day to explore its well stocked antique shops and cafes. Enjoy a country cooked meal, before returning to Mt Barker in the evening.

field_values.redo_desc_about:
Combine our tour through the sports precinct, stop off at a cafe inside the MCG before finishing off in the interactive Australian Sport Museum.
Starting from the heart of the city we walk along the Yarra River into Melbourne’s world famous sporting precinct exploring over 150 years of sports history ranging from the Olympics, cricket, Australian football, rugby, tennis through to horseracing, F1, surfing and golf.
Take a break at a cafe inside the MCG styled on Melbourne’s famous coffee scene and enjoy a beverage and something sweet as you look out on to the famous arena.
You will finish with a guided tour inside the amazing Australian Sports Museum. Dedicated to all Australian sports, it is no ordinary museum and is unlike any other sports museum in the world. It has recently undergone a multi-million dollar transformation to make it more interactive and to update all of its exhibitions.

- Wander through Melbourne Park and Rod Laver Arena and learn about the history of the Australian Open
- Visit venues that host Australian Rules football, soccer, tennis, rowing, rugby league, and more
- Learn about Melbourne's range of world class events such as the Melbourne Cup, F1 Grand Prix, MotoGP, and Bells Beach Surf Pro
- Discover why Melbourne has been voted the Sporting Capital of the World

field_values.redo_desc_about:
Sparsely populated - save for the wildlife who call this rugged coastline home - the Catlins in the southern tip of the South Island offers views of some of New Zealand’s most stunning natural beauty. Your tour begins at 8am from your accommodation as we head south along the Southern Scenic route, through the sea-side village of Brighton before stopping for photos at the mouth of the mighty Taieri River. Continuing on you will go through Waihola and Balclutha before arriving in Owaka, the gateway to the Catlins. Your first short walk takes you to Nugget Point, the most iconic landform of the Otago Coastline. From here you will see the several rugged rocks likened to gold nuggets where NZ fur seals and many NZ seabirds can be viewed. If you visit between December and February there is always the chance of seeing a huge Elephant Seal from the viewing platform. Continuing south our next stop is at a picturesque bay known to be a favourite haul-out site for the rarest sea lion in the world, the New Zealand sea lion. After being hunted to near extinction, only about 200 remain on the mainland. Stand in awe of their magnificence, you’ll be as close as 10 metres from one of these wonderful marine mammals. Driving through native coastal rainforest surrounded by ancient trees your next short walk takes you to the highest waterfall in the Catlins. Your guide will introduce you to several native bush birds and native plants before you arrive at the McLean Falls, arguably the most spectacular of all the waterfalls in the Catlins. Further south you will get the opportunity to look for one of the rarest and smallest dolphins in the world – the Hectors dolphin. The nutrient-rich waters attract this dolphin to become resident in one of the bays on the Catlins coast during the warmer months. You will be taken to the best vantage points to look for these dolphins while your guide prepares light refreshments. Your last stop is at a 180 million year old petrified forest that is revealed at low tide. The fossilised remains of an ancient forest can clearly be seen, representing one of only three accessible sites in the world. Depending on your travel arrangements, our guide can drop you off when the tour ends at 6pm in Invercargill, the Stewart Island Ferry Terminal or take you back to your accommodation in Dunedin.
*Departure times can vary depending on the arrival/departure times of visiting cruise ships and will be confirmed during the booking process.
If you have any concerns please contact us*

You are in for an exceptional Great Barrier Reef adventure with Rum Runner who specializes in Cairns Great Barrier Reef experiences, catering to swimmers and snorkelers, those wanting to try an introductory dive (no experience necessary) and certified scuba divers of all experience levels.
So keep a close eye on our booking page for our departure dates during the week.
Each site your dive will be unique, allowing you to explore vast coral gardens, walls and isolated pinnacles, while amazing you with the sheer diversity and colour of marine life.

If you can make your tank last that long, go for it!
Or if you’re quick on your air, come back for a short refill and jump back in.
We will let you know what time you need to be back for lunch.
The second site we visit is a unique Sand Cay in the middle of a vast Coral Garden.

description: Enjoy a choice of two reef locations, classic yacht and a friendly professional team to look after you

You are in for an exceptional Great Barrier Reef adventure with Rum Runner who specializes in Cairns Great Barrier Reef experiences, catering to swimmers and snorkelers, those wanting to try an introductory dive (no experience necessary) and certified scuba divers of all experience levels.

DEPARTURE INFORMATION

Departure is from Marlin Marina, E finger, Cairns at 7:00am to the Outer South Eastern Coral fields and cays, on selected days when we know you’re going to have the best weather conditions for the week! So keep a close eye on our booking page for our departure dates during the week.

2 different dive and snorkel sites
Special Prices start from $220.00
Returns to Cairns at 6pm

THE DIVING

Each site your dive will be unique, allowing you to explore vast coral gardens, walls and isolated pinnacles, while amazing you with the sheer diversity and colour of marine life. Rum Runner offers you the freedom to dive with your buddy or join a guided dive with one of our dive crew at no extra cost!

During your Rum Runner full day tour, you have the option of taking up to two dives at the two reef sites we visit. The first site allows for unlimited snorkel and dive time of up to 120 minutes. If you can make your tank last that long, go for it! Or if you’re quick on your air, come back for a short refill and jump back in. We will let you know what time you need to be back for lunch.

The second site we visit is a unique Sand Cay in the middle of a vast Coral Garden. Dive here or snorkel over to the cay and walk on a sand island in the middle of the ocean.
Tour includes dive quality masks and fins. Wetsuits are available in all sizes and include 3mm full length.

Rum Runner offers a tanks and weight rate for Scuba divers bringing their own scuba equipment. Top quality scuba equipment, including dive computers available for hire.
Departing 3pm from the sand cay, enjoy a relaxing sunset sail and cruise on deck. BYO your own beer and wine. Returns Cairns 6pm.

field_values.redo_desc_about: Melbourne's Night Photography Workshop is a fun photography course running from dusk for 2 hours. The Night Photography Workshop runs for 2 hours and will teach you great tips on how to take stunning night photos. The course runs in small groups of 6 or less so you receive lots of 1 on 1 help. We use manual settings on your camera so you can be in full control of your camera to obtain the results you want. The course is designed for you to learn a range of settings for all different types of night photography. You'll be given the knowledge to be able to capture anything at night from fireworks to night portraits. We run this photography course under the close guidance of your photography teacher who has over 20 years of experience in the industry.

2 hours

The Night Photography Workshop runs for 2 hours and will teach you great tips on how to take stunning night photos. The course runs in small groups of 6 or less so you receive lots of 1 on 1 help. The course is designed for you to learn a range of settings for all different types of night photography. 234963.raw_booking:
Your booking for Melbourne's Night Photography Workshop is confirmed. Please aim to arrive at least 5 minutes early.

Our two-hour Night Photography Workshop is designed to teach you how to improve your photographic skills with a focus on night photography. 

We’ll start our workshop just before dusk. You will spend time photographing Melbourne's gorgeous city lights, experimenting with some creative applications using long exposures and learning how to take spectacular images in low light. 

[Click here to download your photography notes as a PDF](https://cdn.filestackcontent.com/we9ox9PvTyLShS2fulbe)
 If you would like a hard copy version, please advise by email and I’ll organise this for you.

##Please bring:

field_values.redo_desc_about:
#Course includes a full day diving at beautiful Rottnest Island.
The Advanced scuba diving course is a full-on 2-day course in a small group of 8 students. It is composed of 5 dives. With the PADI Advanced Open Water course, students are going to cover 5 adventure dives with a theme for each one. Among those dives, we will have to do a Deep Dive and Navigation Dive. You will discuss the other dives options with your instructor. On the second day, we enjoy two dives at Rottnest Island with our private charter vessel Linni.
We also now offer the Option to do your Enriched Air Course (Nitrox). At a discounted price, you can improve your scuba diving experience, with this course. Stay underwater longer, feel less tired and get more knowledge about Scuba Diving.
field_values.redo_desc_highlights:
Thanks to the PADI Advanced Open Water course, you will gain new skills:
- Navigate with and without compass
- Dive to 30 metres with an equally qualified buddy
- Explore the Underwater World at night time
But this higher-level course is not only about getting deeper. Our objective is to give your more confidence in your own skills so you can join new activities underwater. Among them, you could dive in the drift current of Komodo Island or explore the dive wreck in Western Australia.
field_values.redo_desc_requirements:
- Open Water Diver (PADI or any other agency)
- 15 years old
- Complete a medical form
- You will need to have your own additional gear of slate, SMB and dive knife (available to purchase at the shop for a discounted price)
- Access to your own car (we can organise car sharing if requested)
field_values.redo_meeting_point: East Street Jetty, Beach Street, East Fremantle, Perth, WA 6160
field_values.redo_booking_what_to_bring:

field_values.redo_desc_about:
We take you to see the Governor Generals' residence from the lake and present a well researched commentary on some of the early European history of the area. Our guests are frequently surprised about some of the information we share on this cruise. Join us for a relaxing leisurely cruise along a section of the lake which is less frequently traveled. The area has an amassing history, of both the original indigenous folk and the early European settlers. The owner and operator of Lake Burley Griffin Cruises is Jim Paterson, who has lived in Canberra with his wife Virginia since the early 1980s. Jim had a long and successful career in broadcasting and television before turning his attention to the water in 2003. His entertaining and well-researched commentary is one of the highlights of your lake cruise. The Boats; Our first boat Cygnet was converted from the steam launch Jenny and commenced service in 2003. It’s a replica Edwardian style electric launch. Cygnet was the first commercial all electric vessel on Lake Burley Griffin, and the uniquely quiet ride adds an extra element of tranquillity to the cruise. The MV Gull commenced service in October 2009, increasing the passenger carrying capacity and enhancing our range of services. In 2012 Gull was converted to all electric. Both electric boats are running on green energy charging their batteries overnight.
It provides an other perspective on your National Capital.
The boats run on green energy to provide carbon neutral transportation, a positive contribution to the environment.

field_values.redo_desc_about:
#Two Rivers, Twice the Excitement!
Combining two of the most exciting rivers in New Zealand for an epic day of Rafting!!
Start the day off conquering the wild Wairoa river in Tauranga, The best grade 5 River in NZ with intense rapids and boulder gardens this is not for the faint hearted!
Followed by a quick lunch stop we then take on the almighty Kaituna River, home to the highest commercial waterfall rafted in the world at a whopping 7 meters!!
Full day of rafting madness!!!
field_values.redo_desc_highlights:
Conquer the Finest Rivers in the Bay in Just One Day!
This action-packed adventure is not for the faint of heart, as it promises thrills and excitement that will keep you energized for days!

field_values.redo_desc_itinerary:
8:00 AM - Departure
From our rafting base located at 18 Okere Falls Road. *Please arrive early!*
9:30 AM - Arrival
At the starting point on the Wairoa River.
Jump into our rafting gear, receive training, and prepare to conquer the rapids!
On the River
We will be out on the water for approximately 1.5 hours, with a brief stop for snacks and restroom breaks on the way back to our base.
2:00 PM - Arrival at Base
You will have time to eat and recharge before the next adventure at 2:30 PM.
2:30 PM - Kaituna River Journey
We get ready, undergo training, and set off once more.
Expect to spend about an hour on the Kaituna River, returning to base around 4:30 PM.

Followed by a quick lunch stop we then take on the almighty Kaituna River, home to the highest commercial waterfall rafted in the world at a whopping 7 meters!!

Full day of rafting madness!!!

- Lifejacket
- Splash Jackets
- Fleece Top

itinerary: 8:00 AM - Departure
From our rafting base located at 18 Okere Falls Road. *Please arrive early!*

9:30 AM - Arrival
At the starting point on the Wairoa River.
Jump into our rafting gear, receive training, and prepare to conquer the rapids!

On the River
We will be out on the water for approximately 1.5 hours, with a brief stop for snacks and restroom breaks on the way back to our base.

2:00 PM - Arrival at Base
You will have time to eat and recharge before the next adventure at 2:30 PM.

2:30 PM - Kaituna River Journey
We get ready, undergo training, and set off once more.
Expect to spend about an hour on the Kaituna River, returning to base around 4:30 PM.

highlights: Conquer the Finest Rivers in the Bay in Just One Day!

This action-packed adventure is not for the faint of heart, as it promises thrills and excitement that will keep you energized for days!

faqs: Q. Do need to know how to swim?
A. For the Wairoa river you must have strong swimming skills - please choose the Kaituna river of not 

Q. Are there changing facilities?
A. We do have a small changing tent but do recommend arriving in your swimwear already. 

Q. Toilets?
A. As we only raft here 26 days a year we don't have a base set up, sometimes there is a portaloo out there but again, we recommend using the restroom before arrival

#Walking the track

The Milford Track starts at Glade Wharf, Te Anau Downs. Free car parking is available at Te Anau Downs, or bus transfers can also be booked from Queenstown or central Te Anau.

After 4 days tramping through beautiful beech forests and across alpine passes, the track ends with a short boat ride from Sandfly Point to Milford Sound. RealNZ operate only the boat service at the end of the track and this must be booked in advance. 

#What's included

- Boat transfer from Te Anau Downs to track start - Departs at 10:30am or 2:00pm (Day 1)
- Boat shuttle from Sandfly Point to Milford Sound at the end of the hike on Day 4. There will be multiple daily departures between 2pm and 4.30pm

##What to bring
Personal medication, including for asthma and allergies

##Important Information:
Milford Sounds natural beauty captivates all who visit, but it also comes with its share of natural hazards. Visit [our website](https://www.realnz.com/en/plan/natural-hazard/) for full information about hazards and risks in the area.

Be sure to stay informed about road conditions by checking the NZTA website [here](https://www.nzta.govt.nz/projects/sh94-milford-road/). In the winter months, remember to carry snow chains and be ready for possible delays.

For more information, please freephone 0800 4 HIGHWAYS (0800 44 44 49), which is available 24/7.

##Cruise Information

Please arrive at least 15 min prior to your scheduled departure time and present your ticket(s) with your QR Code(s) to the Fantasea Cruising boat crew at the departure wharf.

Your cruise will depart from **Manly Wharf 2** at 11:30AM. **Boarding will begin at 11:15AM.** 

The cruise will leave at 11:30AM sharp as we are unable to remain at the wharf past this time. We ask that you allow ample time to arrive at the wharf.

Your cruise is BYO food with a licensed bar onboard. Please only use soft pack portable coolers if you plan on bringing your own food.

# Boxing Day Cruise Comfort Tips 

Subject to weather and sea conditions we will be heading for the **open ocean** during your Boxing Day Cruise, and some passengers may be affected by **motion sickness**. 

Speak to your doctor or pharmacist before the cruise about a motion sickness remedy appropriate for you. 

---

## For Your Comfort 

- The vessel may move due to sea and swell 
- Eat only a light meal before your trip 
- Avoid large meals before or during the voyage 
- Rest well the night before 
- If prone to motion sickness, purchase medication beforehand and take it **well before boarding** 
- The most stable, comfortable area is at the back of the vessel on the lower deck 
- The most movement is at the front of the main cabin, on the front deck, and inside the upper cabin 
- Stay out of bathrooms if feeling unwell 
- Bring warm layers, sunscreen, and a camera 

---

# Cruise Safety and Conduct Guidelines 

To ensure a safe and enjoyable experience for everyone on board, please follow these guidelines: 

## Follow Crew Instructions 
All participants must follow the guidelines and instructions provided by the crew at all times. 

## Moving Around the Boat 
1. Use both hands to hold railings or stable surfaces 
2. Be mindful of trip hazards and slippery surfaces 
3. Avoid moving around if the sea is rough or the weather is windy 
4. Exercise extra caution when using stairs; keep your hands free to hold the handrails 

## Child Supervision 
Children must be supervised by a responsible adult at all times.

**If you have any questions please feel free to ask, either by emailing info@fantasea.com.au or calling us on 1800 326 822, otherwise we hope you enjoy your cruise!**

field_values.redo_desc_about: Discover the very best of Wellington on this action-packed 5-hour guided tour showcasing the capital’s most iconic sights and hidden gems.
field_values.redo_desc_highlights:
- Mt Victoria Lookout – Take in panoramic views over Wellington and the harbour.
- Coastal Adventure – Journey along Oriental Parade, explore the Miramar Peninsula, and experience the dramatic rugged south coast.
- Seaside Lunch Stop – Relax and enjoy lunch at a charming coastal café.
- Brooklyn Wind Turbine - This iconic site combines clean energy innovation with awe-inspiring scenery.
- City Highlights – Visit Wellington’s must-sees, including the Wētā Cave, Wellington Cable Car, Botanical Gardens, and Old St Paul’s Cathedral (optional).
field_values.redo_desc_what_included: Savour a relaxing lunch (mains and a drink included) at one of Wellington’s charming seaside cafés or restaurants, soaking up coastal views and local atmosphere.
field_values.redo_desc_what_excluded: Wellington Cable Car (optional, ticket not included). Visit Old St Paul’s Cathedral (optional, entry $5 NZD per person).
field_values.redo_desc_itinerary:
**09:30-10:00 AM – Tour pickups**
**10:00-10:30 AM - Mt Victoria Lookout**
Begin your day with a scenic drive along the picturesque Wellington Waterfront and Oriental Bay, admiring the elegant seaside homes and the quirky private cable cars that scale Wellington’s steep hillsides, before ascending to Mt Victoria Lookout, where panoramic 360-degree views showcase the city, harbour, and surrounding hills — a perfect introduction to New Zealand’s capital.
**10:50 AM – “Blown Away” Sign Photo Stop**
Pause for a quick photo opportunity at Wellington’s iconic “Blown Away” sign, a playful nod to the city’s famously breezy weather.
**11:00-11:15 AM – Visit the Weta Cave, Miramar**
Continue to Miramar for a visit to the world-renowned Weta Cave Shop — the public gateway to Weta Workshop. Discover the magic of movie-making with a short documentary, explore the mini museum, and take photos with incredible life-sized sculptures from films like The Lord of the Rings and Avatar.
(Note: This stop includes time to browse the shop and museum but does not include a Weta Workshop tour.)
**11:30-12:15 PM – Seaside Lunch Stop**
Savour a relaxing lunch (mains and a drink included) at one of Wellington’s charming seaside cafés or restaurants, soaking up coastal views and local atmosphere.
**12:30 PM – Wahine Memorial Park & South Coast Exploration**
After lunch, visit the Wahine Memorial Park, commemorating one of New Zealand’s most tragic maritime disasters. Continue your journey along Wellington’s rugged South Coast, exploring the Taputeranga Marine Reserve and Te Kopahou Reserve Visitors Centre — where wild coastline and sweeping views meet fascinating natural history.
**1:30-2:00 PM – Brooklyn Wind Turbine Lookout**
Travel inland to the Brooklyn Wind Turbine, one of Wellington’s landmarks, offering spectacular panoramic views over the city and harbour.
**2:15-2:45 PM – Wellington Cable Car & Botanical Gardens**
Return to the city for a chance to experience the Wellington Cable Car (optional, ticket not included). Stroll through the beautifully landscaped Botanic Gardens, finishing at the Lady Norwood Rose Gardens, home to more than 100 rose varieties in bloom during summer.
**2:45-3:00 PM – Parliament Buildings & Old St Paul’s Cathedral**
Drive by (or, time permitting, walk through) the Parliament precinct, including the famous Beehive. If time allows, visit Old St Paul’s Cathedral (optional, entry $5 NZD per person) — a stunning example of Gothic Revival architecture built entirely from native timbers and adorned with exquisite stained-glass windows.
**3:00 PM – Hotel/Cruise terminal drop-offs**

field_values.redo_desc_about: Visit one of New Zealand’s Geothermal wonders situated in the Whakarewarewa on a half day tour from Auckland City. Te Puia Geothermal Valley Rotorua is an active geothermal wonderland! This 60-hectare site is home to the New Zealand Maori Arts and Crafts Institute, alive kiwi enclosure, the world-famous Pohutu Geyser, and more than 500 natural geothermal wonders. Tour starts with us picking you up from Auckland CBD; then you enjoy a three-hour scenic drive towards the Bay of Plenty. On arrival, you will be welcomed by the Māori residents and offered to choose your steam box meal (extra cost) to be cooked in Woven baskets and placed in the active steam vent. After that; your tour guide will take you through a 60 mins tour around 60 hectares of Te Puia Geothermal Valley including the largest active geyser in the Southern Hemisphere, the Pohutu Geyser. You can also See the native Kiwi bird, Mud Pools, watch New Zealand’s iconic native Carvings and Weaving performed in front of you, as well as Learning about the Māori Culture while performing at the sacred Marae. After you finish your amazing experience we make our way back to Auckland CBD.
field_values.redo_desc_what_included:
* Pick up from Auckland CBD
* Snacks & water
* Admission & Guided tour in Te Puia
* Kiwi Bird Watching
* Puhuto Geyser, Mud Pools, Maori Village, Glimpse of Maori Haka performance, National Wood & Stone carving school
* Drive Back to Auckland CBD

field_values.redo_desc_about:
The Coromandel Peninsula was formerly known largely for its Hardrock Gold Mining and Kauri industries but is now a mecca for tourism, especially ecotourism.
Enjoy a Boat Ride to the coastal islands of the marine reserve, reefs, massive sea caves, and bays, including the world-famous Cathedral Cove, Blowholes, and Narnia film locations with an opportunity to see marine life ex. dolphins, seals & little blue penguins (not guaranteed).
The magnificence of this natural Volcanic Scenery is legendary, and the approach by sea, combined with an insightful commentary, further enhances the experience.
Join a 1-hour Train Ride on the Driving Creek Railway that climbs up the hill to the Eyeful Tower. At the top, you will be fascinated by the panoramic views over the island-studded Hauraki Gulf.
Dig a private pool at the famous Hot Water Beach for a unique experience of your own natural spa pool. There are two fissures at Hot Water Beach issuing water as hot as 64C (147F) at a rate as high as 15 litres/minute. This water contains large amounts of salt (NOT salt water), calcium, magnesium, potassium, fluorine, bromine, and silica.

field_values.redo_desc_about: Experience the very best of Auckland city as well as the Waitakere Ranges on Auckland’s famous West Coast on a small group in one spectacular day. Enjoy this full day tour with TIME Unlimited Tours, winner of multiple global awards including the National Geographic World Legacy award. Enjoy an amazing full day experience including lunch with the very best overview of Auckland City and its glorious West Coast. Marvel at views of several ancient volcanoes on the Auckland isthmus. Travel through the Auckland Domain with the Auckland Museum as its centrepiece, stopping to enjoy views of Auckland’s 2nd-largest volcano. Continue through the boutique suburb of Parnell, restored in the old colonial style and with many beautiful mansions. Explore Tamaki Drive, one of the world’s most beautiful city drives, along Auckland’s waterfront, looking out at several of the stunning beaches along Auckland's shoreline. See Mission Bay, arguably Auckland’s most well-known beach with lovely golden sand. Enjoy great views of the famous Hauraki Gulf and the mystical island volcano Rangitoto Island, Auckland’s largest and youngest volcano at 600 years old. Drive over the iconic Auckland Harbour Bridge, spanning the sparkling blue waters of the Waitemata Harbour dotted with white sails, from which you can marvel at the iconic view back to Auckland’s skyline. Visit the Arataki Visitor Centre at the gateway to Te Wao Nui o Tiriwa, the great forest of the Maori ancestor Tiriwa, also known as the Waitakere Ranges. Witness spectacular ocean vistas of both the Manukau Harbour and along Auckland’s wild West Coast. Get up close to some of New Zealand’s unique indigenous flora and fauna. View soaring cliffs, roaring surf and spectacular volcanic black sand beaches. Discover ancient native rainforest including our New Zealand Christmas Trees (Pohutukawa), Nikau Palms, our national icon the Silver Fern, plus our amazing Kauri Trees.
field_values.redo_desc_what_included: Fully guided service in Mercedes luxury vehicle. Pick-up/drop-off within Auckland’s Downtown area including cruise wharf (for airport pick-up or drop-off please refer to our private tours). Complimentary snacks, water and lunch also included. 2-15 passengers shared, small group tour basis.

field_values.redo_desc_about:
The Waitomo Caves, which are located about 2 ½ hours south of Auckland, is one of New Zealand’s most famous attractions. On this tour we travel via New Zealand’s famous Thermal Explorer Highway touring route, taking in the special region of Hamilton through the beautiful countryside of the Waikato and King Country.
As we drive southward, we show you sacred Taupiri Mountain as well as Ngaruawahia, the site of the famous Turangawaewae Marae (Maori meeting place) and seat of New Zealand’s Maori King. At Waitomo you will experience one of their amazing tours to explore the underground wonderland that is Waitomo Caves. The most popular option is the world-famous Waitomo Glowworm Caves on a 45 minute tour, which includes a boat ride on an underground stream to view the magically dazzling glowworms. There are other caving options too, such as Cave Tubing / Black Water Rafting. Here you can float, walk and swim along underground waterways on a big, inflated tube. This is for the more adventurous and is great fun!
On our private luxury tours, we offer the various Waitomo caving options separately to our private tour since we have found our guests like to be able to book the caving option they prefer – whether that is a gentle tour or an adventurous tour to explore the caves. However, we can certainly incorporate these into your booking with us. An option is also to visit the nearby Kiwi House in Otorohanga, where you can see the Kiwi, our national bird and emblem, as well as many of our flora and fauna. Please let us know if you would like us to incorporate this option. Return to Auckland at the end of a magnificent day exploring this world-famous part of New Zealand.
field_values.redo_desc_what_included: Fully guided tour in Mercedes luxury vehicle. Pick-up/drop-off in Auckland incl airport/cruise terminal. Entry to Waitomo Glowworm Caves GROUP Tour. Complimentary snacks, water and lunch also included.

field_values.redo_desc_about: Join us for a unique and exclusive Wellington sightseeing experience. Shenandoah, one of our favourite Wellington tours and exclusive to Xplor Tours, takes you to perhaps the best but least known destination in the region. Approximately 20 minutes’ drive from Wellington, overlooking the sparkling Pauatahanui Inlet and linked with Battle Hill (a significant Maori War site), Shenandoah is a working farm and hidden historical gem inside a native wild birdlife reserve. Once Xplor Tours drops you there, owner and proud Kiwi Simon takes you on a unique and magical tour around his beautiful, relaxing property, and through its history. Originally a Maori Fortress Pa for Ngati Toa in the 1800’s, the property has seen three different owners over 150 years. After withstanding a major battle with English troops, it became a Crown Fort to guard the stagecoach road from highway robbers. Some of the first settlers to New Zealand made contact with the local iwi here, before the whalers and settlers transformed Pauatahanui into the thriving rural community of today. Early in World War II, Shenandoah was commandeered as a US Marine training base and housed over 100,000 troops, ushering in the next military episode of the site. The history isn’t just told in stories though; behind the barn doors, a private museum is filled with artifacts found on the property which date back over the last 150 years. As part of your day trip to Shenandoah with Xplor Tours, you can relax by the pond and jetty or other seating areas in the gardens, and enjoy a tea or coffee with morning or afternoon tea. Simon’s passion and ability to enthral makes this Wellington tour experience genuinely unique and one that will stay with you long after you leave Shenandoah. Come on a Shenandoah tour with Xplor Tours and you will see why “Pauatahanui” means “the place you never want to leave from.”

Rich in local history, from the Maori Wars through to WWII.
Collections of rare vintage examples of a certain well-known marque of American motorbikes.

Experiencing the history of an area in a living museum complete with the personal stories of the people involved.
Enjoying refreshments in a beautiful, scenic and relaxing location.

field_values.redo_desc_about: Combine a luxury transfer from Rotorua to Auckland with a visit to 2 world-famous attractions in New Zealand: Hobbiton Movie Set and Waitomo Glowworm Caves. After pick-up in Rotorua, we drive across the Mamaku Plateau to the Hobbiton Movie Set near the rural town of Matamata, made world-famous as the original setting of Sir Peter Jackson’s “The Lord of the Rings” and “The Hobbit” trilogies. On the 2-hour tour of the Hobbiton Movie Set, get astonishing insights into how these movies were made and which parts of the movies were filmed here. Not only movie fans will enjoy this unique experience with inside views of the Hobbit village including Hobbit Holes, Bag End, The Green Dragon Inn and astonishing facts about the filmmaking and spectacular landscape all around. We then continue on to Waitomo Caves, located in the King Country in the Waikato region. On this tour we travel via the Thermal Explorer Highway touring route, taking in the special region as we drive through the beautiful countryside of New Zealand’s North Island. At Waitomo, experience the underground wonderland that is Waitomo Glowworm Caves with thousands of Glowworms as the major attraction. As we drive northward on the journey from Waitomo to Auckland, we show you sacred Taupiri Mountain as well as Ngaruawahia, the site of Turangawaewae Marae (Maori meeting place) and seat of New Zealand’s Maori King. Be dropped off in Auckland after combining a transfer from Rotorua to Auckland with exploring some of the most beautiful parts of Aotearoa / New Zealand. This Private One-Way Tour from Rotorua via Waitomo Glowworm Caves and Hobbiton Movie Set to Auckland allows you to see 2 of New Zealand’s most famous attractions in one amazing day.
field_values.redo_desc_what_included: Fully guided Private Tour in Mercedes luxury vehicle. Pick-up Rotorua and drop-off Auckland. Complimentary snacks, water and lunch. Entry fees to Waitomo Caves and Hobbiton Movie Set GROUP Tours. All tours support local eco-cultural initiatives.

field_values.redo_desc_about: Enjoy a leisurely three hour cruise on our solar electric ferry from Elizabeth Quay in the heart of our city. We cruise quietly along showing off our beautiful city and river. We pass the Crown Casino, cruise under the Matagarup Bridge and Optus Stadium and up through some of the most scenic country side flanking our river as it winds its way up to the Swan River. Three hours after departing Elizabeth Quay we have you disembarking at Sandalford Winery [adjacent to Mandoon Estate] where you can relax and enjoy the magnificent facilities of these wineries.. luncheon, wine tastings and more. We arrange an Uber trip back into the city at your preferred time - its all part and parcel of this unique offering.

field_values.redo_desc_about: This compact, easygoing guided taster explores the northern end of the Western Bays from Kinloch Marina, combining coastal and bush scenery. Over one and a half hours you’ll cruise between dramatic coastal cascades, hop off at two waterfalls reachable only by boat, and take a short five-minute bush walk to a third. The outing is ideal for nature lovers and photographers seeking striking waterfall views and an evening sunset from the lake without a long trek.
field_values.redo_desc_highlights:
* Dramatic coastal cascades and waterfall visits
* Three waterfall viewpoints including two accessed from the water
* Short walk combined with relaxed boat cruising—ideal for photographers
* Enjoy the ride back with the setting sun
field_values.redo_desc_itinerary:
1. Cruise from Kinloch Marina along the northern Western Bays coastline.
2. Hop off at two waterfalls accessible from the water.
3. Take a short five-minute bush walk to a third waterfall.
4. Return cruise to Kinloch Marina.
field_values.redo_desc_requirements: Please contact staff to discuss options.
field_values.redo_desc_check_in: Please arrive 5 minutes prior to departure for boarding. Free all-day parking is available at our berth, located at 10 Kinloch Esplanade, Kinloch.
field_values.redo_desc_other: Seasonal departure times vary: Sept to Nov at 6pm, Dec to Jan at 7pm, Feb to Mar at 6pm.
field_values.redo_booking_what_to_bring: Layer up! Taupo can be very cold, especially if the sun isn’t shining or there’s the slightest breeze. We recommend wearing layers of clothing. It is much better to take layers off than it is to not have enough to put on!
field_values.redo_booking_location: berth 37, Kinloch Marina (At the end of Kinloch Esplanade - not Mata Place)
field_values.redo_booking_check_in: show us this email on the day you arrive
field_values.redo_booking_departure_info: 10 minutes prior to your departure time
field_values.redo_booking_cancellation: In extreme cases we may cancel your trip due to weather. Should that happen a full refund will be given.

Unfortunately, the weather on the lake is unpredictable. In extreme cases we may cancel your trip due to weather. Should that happen a full refund will be given.

Regards
The Venture Beyond team

field_values.redo_desc_about: An alpine pass, and a pristine mountain lake. All within easy reach of Christchurch. What more could you ask for? At a little over 930m this is a highest point on SH 73, which links Canterbury to the West Coast, even higher than the better know Arthurs Pass! An added bonus is Lake Lyndon on the other side of the pass.
field_values.redo_desc_what_included:
- Pickup from some of the main hotels within Christchurch, or alternately from the Canterbury Museum
- Expert, knowledgeable guide
- Photography tuition (if required)
- Late model, air conditioned transport
- Snacks, beverages, and drinks
- Scenic stops
field_values.redo_desc_itinerary:
Join us as we head west out of Christchurch straight for the Southern Alps foothills via the scenic Canterbury Plains before we make a first stop at Aylesbury Corner to take advantage of the scenic lookout platform. If we’re there at the right time we may even get to see one of the massive coal trains that are coming and going from the West Coast.
From here we continue along the West Coast Rd via Sheffield and Springfield to our next stop where we stretch our legs once more and enjoy the mountainous vistas opening up in front of us before resuming our westward journey into the foothills, taking on the increasingly steep climb up Porters Pass followed by a dizzying descent down the other side to Lake Lyndon where we stop for a drink and nibbles while enjoying the scenery and fresh air.
From Lake Lyndon we make our way another 4 km north-west along the West Coast Rd to a lookout point above dry stream with amazing views out over the Porter River and Whitewater Stream towards Castle Hill with Broken Hill and Mt Manson adding to the scene. This is the turn around point for us, but not the end of the tour as we’ve plenty more amazing things to take as we retrace our steps to Christchurch, beginning with Porters Pass itself.
From Porters Pass we gaze upon and admire the alpine views surrounding us; West is Mount Enys and the Craigieburn Range, East is the West Coast road snaking its way down the hill towards the Canterbury Plains, just visible over the tops of the hills ahead of you. Either side of us is Foggy Peak to the north and the slopes of the Kowai Forest and Big Ben range to the south.
Heading back towards Christchurch we detour across the Waimakariri Gorge Bridge for a last stop but one (time permitting) admiring the historic bridge and the river gorge it crosses before continuing along South Eyre Rd to the North Canterbury town of Kaiapoi for that final picturesque stop on the banks of the Waimakariri River Regional Park, before winding up our trip back in the city.

field_values.redo_desc_about: Join us on a 5 day excursion deep into Southland, and we’ll throw a side-trip into Milford Sound into the package for you. Not to mention the unspoiled Catlins Coast. A longish one this time, but worth it! From Christchurch we head inland to Queenstown before dipping further South to Te Anau and into Milford Sound for that obligatory nature cruise on the Fiord. From Te Anau we work our way into Invercargill and then the Catlins Coast in the South-East corner of the island before turning North for Dunedin and eventually our starting point in Christchurch.

- Pickup from some of the main hotels within Christchurch, or alternately from the Canterbury Museum

field_values.redo_desc_itinerary:
###Day 1:
Christchurch to Queenstown: Today we head to Queenstown via Lake Tekapo, Omarama, and Cromwell. And of course, Aoraki Mt Cook! Enjoy stunning views of lakes with mountain backdrops, land locked valleys, mountain passes, and narrow valleys
###Day 2:
Queenstown to Milford Sound and Te Anau: Early start as we head to Milford Sound with numerous stops to enjoy and photograph the scenery before arriving in Milford Sound for a scenic cruise on the fiord. More stops to explore the environment on our way back out to Te Anau
###Day 3:
Te Anau to Invercargill: Weather permitting enjoy an optional 40 min helicopter flight over Fiordland, then salivate over the scenery as we head south past Lake Manapouri. Along the way we detour to look at Lake Monowai, and Lake Hauroko before heading out to the coast at Te Waewae Bay. Following road round through Colac Bay and Riverton, we eventually arrive in Invercargill mid-afternoon. If we have time to spare we explore Oreti beach, and the area around Bluff
###Day 4:
Invercargill to Dunedin: Travelling to Dunedin “The long way round” via the Catlins Conservation Park is like a step back in time. Explore and photograph beautiful waterfalls, the remains of a petrified forest, and coastal islets before rejoining SH 1 at Balclutha. Turning off SH 1, we then detour out to the coast once again, this time to the Taieri River Mouth before following the coast as far as Waldronville and arriving in Dunedin in time to explore the Otago Harbour area
###Day 5:
Dunedin to Christchurch: Further exploration of Otago Harbour is a must before working our way north towards Christchurch. Once again we enjoy and soak-up coastal scenery, as far as Oamaru with its Steam-punk scene, and Timaru’s scenic waterfront at Caroline Bay, before regrettably arriving back at our starting point in the garden city.

field_values.redo_desc_about: This fantastic Eco tour begins at your hotel and the historical Rocks area of old Sydney. Heading westwards across the coastal plain we make our way to the Great Dividing Range of Australia. Our first stop today is Featherdale; this unique park gives visitors the opportunity to discover over three hundred different varieties of unique Australian wildlife. Reboarding the vehicle we continue west towards the Blue Mountains National Park. We enter a little known hidden clearing to enjoy some home style morning tea. You will have time to roam the area and seek out the wild kangaroos and birdlife that frequents this part of the National Park. Next we visit some scenic lookouts to view the Blue Mountains such as King’s Tableland, Eagle Hawk and Narrow Neck lookout, enjoy the stunning sights of the three sisters as you overlook the magnificent Jamison Valley. Lunch today is at the charming village of Leura. Here you will have a chance to stroll the main street before settling down at the delightful Leura Garage Cafe. Enjoy fresh and healthy local produce in the funky surrounds of a converted garage. After lunch we skirt around cliff drive towards the township of Katoomba. At Eagle Hawk lookout you will see the famous 3 sisters Rock formation and marvel at the stunning views of the Jamieson Valley. From here we continue around Narrowneck Plateau for more incredible vantage points. This afternoon we travel to the scenic Evan’s Lookout for more gorgeous views of the Blue Mountains and finish the day with a visit to Scenic World and the famous Scenic Rail, a four hundred and fifteen meter decent through the cliff side tunnel will take you into the ancient rainforest itself. From here you are free to explore the area before rejoining the vehicle once more and making our way back to Sydney.
field_values.redo_desc_highlights: Highly qualified and knowledgeable guide, travel in luxury air-conditioned vehicles, morning tea and coffee, lunch, city hotel pick up and drop off, comprehensive commentary, entry into Blue Mountains National Park, Entry into Featherdale Wildlife Park, Entry into Scenic World.
field_values.redo_desc_what_included: Morning tea, entry to Featherdale, Ultimate Discovery Pass at Scenic World, café style lunch including one glass of beer, wine or softdrink!

field_values.redo_desc_about: Less than an hour’s drive to the west of Melbourne is the stunning Yarra Valley. The rolling hills and majestic landscape are backdrop to a wonderful food and wine experience. The Yarra Valley is one of several wine destinations in Australia however unique in the fact that it is home to well known Domaine Chandon in Australia. Enjoy a private wine tasting in the famous Green Room situated inside Domaine, or visit any number of other boutique and organic world class cellar doors. Your private guide will tailor an authentic experience to suit you. We depart Melbourne city for the short drive over to the renowned Yarra Valley. As we travel out of the city your guide will provide some background on Australia’s second most populated city. Soon we enter the Yarra Valley. Over 50 wineries are established in the valley, varying in size from small family vineyards to large international establishments. We will take time to show you the best the region has to offer. One of our first winery stops for the day will be at Coldstream Hills. With a reputation for producing outstanding single vineyard and reserve wines Coldstream Hills has a particular focus on the internationally heralded varieties, Chardonnay and Pinot Noir. Next we’ll go to Domaine Chandon – established by French champagne house Moët & Chandon in 1986, this scenic winery set amongst the verdant hills of the Yarra Valley is dedicated to traditional production methods of cool climate still wines. Lunch today is at Yering Station. Set within stunning architecture, this signature restaurant overlooks expansive and magnificent views of the Yarra Ranges. Yering Station’s Head Chef, Laura Webb-James, designs tempting menus making the most of the fresh, seasonal produce available from the region. The afternoon will be ours to enjoy. There are many other wineries on offer or maybe you will prefer a visit to one of the many produce stores. Your guide will make some suggestions to finish up your afternoon. Return to your hotel after a great day amongst the vineyards.
field_values.redo_desc_what_included: Your private guide will collect you from your hotel, 2 course lunch including beer/wine/soft drink, private wine tastings, & general admission into Sanctuary.

field_values.redo_desc_about: Experience Macadamias Australia, a multi-generational family farm located right here in Bundaberg! Macadamias Australia's Orchard Tours deliver an insightful immersion into the world of macadamias and sustainable farming, where visitors learn firsthand about how their passionate team care for the land and manage the quality of their premium, single-origin macadamias; from seed, to tree, to table. This exclusive tour is available for all ages and abilities and will give you an opportunity to discover the humble beginnings of Macadamias Australia and includes a walk through the orchard that surrounds the tourism centre and café. Your personal tour guide will share their wealth of information on Australia’s native nut as well as a tasting experience and virtual look at the processing. Orchard tours operate each Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday in morning and afternoon time slots, with additional scheduling during busy holiday periods.

field_values.redo_desc_other: Macadamias Australia is a third-generation, family owned and operated agribusiness established in 1957 by the Steinhardt family. Known for its perfect climate, enriched soil, plentiful water and clean environment – the family’s farm is located on the east coast of Australia in Bundaberg, Queensland. Macadamias Australia promotes best practice and innovation in growing and value-adding and markets 100% of its production, providing its customers with a consistent and reliable supply of premium quality macadamias with full traceability. Macadamias Australia welcomes guests from all over the world to engage all their senses in an immersive macadamia wonderland that does not stop once the tour is over. The state-of-the-art Visitor Experience also comprises a Farmgate Shop, Chocolate Viewing Room and chef-designed menu from the in-house café, The Orchard Table.

field_values.redo_booking_other:
Macadamias Australia is a third-generation, family owned and operated agribusiness established in 1957 by the Steinhardt family.
The company maintains over 200,000 macadamia trees and promotes best practice and innovation in growing and handling.
Marketing premium-quality macadamias worldwide – Macadamias Australia supplies macadamias kernel to some of the world’s largest food manufacturers, as well as the snack, bakery, ingredient, retail and confectionary industry sectors.
Macadamias Australia is the only International grower that solely markets 100% of its production – providing its customers with a consistent and reliable supply of premium quality macadamias with full traceability.
Known for its perfect climate, enriched soil, plentiful water and clean environment – Macadamias Australia plantations are located on the east coast of Australia in Bundaberg Queensland.
In what are ideal conditions, the company harvests 2000 tonne of ‘nut in shell’ of the Australian native each year, and is one of the largest single variety plantations in Australia – providing its customers with uniformity of product.
The Steinhardt family prides itself on its long-term working relationships with existing customers and welcomes overseas buyers to visit Macadamias Australia to see the family's plantation and drying facilities firsthand.

field_values.redo_desc_about:
Step in for a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to see New Zealand’s iconic Kiwi bird in the wild, thriving in its natural habitat. Led by an expert guide, this immersive evening experience takes you through the predator-free environment of Tāwharanui Regional Park, one of the country’s most successful wildlife sanctuaries. As you explore native bush under the cover of darkness, you will have one of the rarest opportunities in New Zealand to encounter Kiwi birds living freely in the wild while learning about their behaviour, conservation, and the unique ecosystem they call home.
Before your wildlife adventure begins, enjoy a delicious 3-course dinner at Matakana Market Kitchen, beautifully located alongside the picturesque Matakana River. Relax and savour locally inspired cuisine in a welcoming setting before heading out for your unforgettable nocturnal experience.
Combining exceptional dining, stunning natural surroundings, fascinating conservation stories, and the rare privilege of observing Kiwi birds in their natural environment, this unique evening offers an authentic and truly memorable New Zealand experience.
field_values.redo_desc_what_included:
Round-trip luxury transportation from Auckland.
Complimentary refreshments (water, hot chocolate, and cookies) are included.
Free WI-FI on board.

description: Step in for a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to see New Zealand’s iconic Kiwi bird in the wild, thriving in its natural habitat. Led by an expert guide, this immersive evening experience takes you through the predator-free environment of Tāwharanui Regional Park, one of the country’s most successful wildlife sanctuaries. As you explore native bush under the cover of darkness, you will have one of the rarest opportunities in New Zealand to encounter Kiwi birds living freely in the wild while learning about their behaviour, conservation, and the unique ecosystem they call home.

Before your wildlife adventure begins, enjoy a delicious 3-course dinner at Matakana Market Kitchen, beautifully located alongside the picturesque Matakana River. Relax and savour locally inspired cuisine in a welcoming setting before heading out for your unforgettable nocturnal experience.

Combining exceptional dining, stunning natural surroundings, fascinating conservation stories, and the rare privilege of observing Kiwi birds in their natural environment, this unique evening offers an authentic and truly memorable New Zealand experience.

description: #Lizard Encounter - Make your visit to Maru especially memorable by meeting a Shingleback or Blue-Tongue Lizard.
___________________________________

##Rates
**Meet a Lizard** - $35
**Meet a Lizard for a Group of 2** - $60

##Ages (4+ years, under 4 free)
Children under 4 years are able to participate with no charge when accompanying an adult paying to do the Meet a Lizard session.
Children aged 4-12 years must pay and be accompanied by an adult also paying to do the same Meet a Lizard session.

##About
Make your visit to Maru especially memorable by meeting a Shingleback or Blue-Tongue Lizard. Learn about the Lizards by name and character, as you interact with them.

You can take as many photos as you like on your own devices.

NOTE: Animal Interactions are an additional purchase upon Animal Park entry. Please ensure that Maru Entry tickets are purchased in addition to the Meet a Lizard.

**Other Information**
- All interactions are at the keepers discretion and may be unavailable in extreme weather conditions to ensure the welfare and safety of our animals and visitors. If Maru cancels the experience for any reason, an alternative experience or full refund will be offered.
- Animals at Maru have the freedom to choose if and how they interact with visitors during experiences, so up close touching and feeding usually occurs but is not guaranteed.
- All tickets require the Credit/Debit Card along with photo ID and signature of the purchaser, or a valid company email/voucher to be presented upon arrival, otherwise entry will be refused.

**Terms & Conditions**
It is important that you arrive early as the experience will not be delayed and will start at the advertised time. If you are late you will miss out on the experience and refunds will not be provided. Please dress appropriately for the forecast weather on the day. The Keepers have the right to cancel this and all animal experiences due to extreme weather or any other situation they feel may compromise the safety and welfare of the animals and visitors and in that instance a different experience may be offered or a full refund. For safety please wear closed in shoes, no thongs or sandals.

#Welcome aboard your Fantasea Cruising / My Fast Ferry 9pm or Midnight Fireworks Cruise on New Year’s Eve

New Year’s Eve is fast approaching, and we hope you are as excited as we are about being on beautiful Sydney Harbour to experience the world’s most iconic fireworks display. 

With all the hustle and bustle that New Year’s Eve offers, please find some valuable information below to help make your boarding process easier.

##Your Vessel

Your cruise is on our vessel **SeaCat 1**. Please take the time to look at the image of your vessel below as Darling Harbour is a very busy area on New Year’s Eve and there will be many vessels departing on the night.

![SeaCat 1](https://www.fantasea.com.au/wp-content/uploads/sites/1538/2025/12/seacat1.jpg)

##Departure Times

- The departure time of your **9pm Fireworks Cruise** is **19:45** sharp from **Darling Harbour – Pier 26, Berth 2**. 
- The departure time of your **Midnight Fireworks Cruise** is **22:30** sharp from **Darling Harbour – King Street Wharf 9**. 

## Check In

- Please check in at least **120 minutes prior to your scheduled departure time** 
- Please bring a **printed or digital copy of your booking confirmation** and check in with one of our team
- At check in you will receive a **boarding wristband** for your cruise.
- **Check in is available at the Fantasea Cruising Office from 12:00 on Wednesday the 31st of December.**

##Check in location is the Fantasea Cruising Darling Harbour Office at Pier 26 (Directly underneath Helm Bar)

![Darling Harbour](https://www.fantasea.com.au/wp-content/uploads/sites/1538/2025/12/dh_office_map.jpg)

## Fraud Prevention

Please present the credit card that was used to pay for your booking and matching valid photo identification. The name listed on your credit card should match the name listed on your booking.

##Boarding

Please make your way to your departure wharf at least 45 minutes before your scheduled departure time. Fantasea Cruising staff will be on location to manage the queue and may allow less mobile passengers to move to the front.

##What to Bring

- You are welcome to bring along snacks and meals. Some snacks will be available for purchase onboard.
- **No BYO alcohol allowed**. There is a licensed bar on board for alcoholic beverages and soft drinks
- Appropriate clothing for the weather conditions on the night
- Please bring a **printed or digital copy of your booking confirmation** as you may need to show this to security personnel at various access points around Darling Harbour.

##On the Night

More than a million people will be making their way into the city for the celebrations. Please find details on road closures and public transport on New Year’s Eve below to help you plan your night.

- [**Public Transport**](https://www.sydneynewyearseve.com/transport)
- [**Road Closures**](https://www.sydneynewyearseve.com/road-closures/)

We very much look forward to having you on board with us to enjoy what promises to be one of the most spectacular events of the year!

Kind Regards,

The Fantasea Cruising / My Fast Ferry team

Join us for an exhilarating tour through Roebuck Bay on our custom built V8 airboat! Roebuck Bay is full of WW2 and pearling history which our guide will inform you of. Based in the Mid North Coast near Coffs Harbour, NSW, Bellingen Canoe Adventures offers canoe trips to all ages, from beginners to the more advanced! Single, double or triple canoe/kayaks. Comfortable, stable, flat bottomed ….you won’t fall out! They even have footrests and backrests for your comfort. Yourself!

meeting_point: Moreton Bay
description: #The best that Brisbane’s coastline has to offer

## Duration

- 9 Hours

## About

Explore and discover the delights of southern Moreton Bay in an affordable and fun way with Aria Cruises. 

Give yourself and your family, friends and loved ones the gift of sailing the sparkling waters.

Enjoy swimming, standup paddle boarding, boom netting, beach cricket, lounge on an aqua mat or just relax and enjoy the abundant marine life, including dolphins, dugongs and sea turtles you may see along the way. 

Aria Cruises can also customize package deals for work functions, parties, or other group gatherings.

## What to Bring
- What you normally take to the beach: towel, hat, swimmers, sunscreen, sunglasses, and a jacket

## Menu
Morning Tea – biscuits, lamingtons, muffins, seasonal fruit

Lunch – garden salad, pasta salad, potato salad, prawn salad, roast chicken, smoked leg ham, pastrami beef, tasty cheese, fresh bread rolls

Beverages – fully licensed bar available for drink purchases
450521.raw_booking:
COVID-19

Please be reassured that we take the health and safety of our passengers and crew very seriously and you can have confidence when booking and peace of mind knowing that we operate a safe business.

Our COVID-19 plan has been put in place to help protect our passengers and crew members from exposure to and infection from COVID-19.

symptoms of COVID-19 
been in close contact with a confirmed case of coronavirus in the last 14 days 
tested positive within the last 14 days or are waiting on test results 

SAILING ADDRESS 

The Public Pontoon at Raby Bay Harbour Park
146-148 Shore Street West
Cleveland QLD

PARKING

Please avoid parking in the Raby Bay Harbour Side Restaurant precinct as vehicles have been towed in the past at the owners expense. Aria Cruises does not accept responsibility for where you park your car.

TIME TO BE THERE

THINGS TO BRING

IMPORTANT

field_values.redo_desc_about:
It is a full day out (approx 4 hrs of riding plus a lunch break). When you arrive at our property in Coominya, you will be greeted by our fantastic team (two-legged AND four-legged). Once the paperwork is sorted and you have your helmet, we will give you the name of your trusty steed for the day. We will help you onto your horse and give instructions on how to ride our quality and exceptional horses 🐎. The ride to the pub is approx two hours each way and we spend a good amount of time to eat a delicious meal and relax before getting back in the saddle to ride home. We head out along the scenic Brisbane Valley Rail Trail, where we often see koalas & other Aussie wildlife. As we expect all riders to be at least comfortable at a rising trot, we will have opportunities to do so. Those more experienced will have an opportunity to canter (weather permitting) if they wish. Please note that if our staff are concerned about your riding ability, they may ask you NOT to join the faster group. Safety comes first!! If you are not a seasoned rider, you might have some sore parts after a day in the saddle!
Intermediate (able to control a horse at walk, trot, canter outside of an arena)

description: #Novice to experienced riders only. Riders must be able to confidently control a horse at a rising trot and have completed 30+ hours in the saddle.

##Duration 
4 hour 

##About 
It is a full day out (approx 4 hrs of riding plus a lunch break)

*Suitable for novice to experienced riders only*

When you arrive at our property in Coominya, you will be greeted by our fantastic team (two-legged AND four-legged). Once the paperwork is sorted and you have your helmet, we will give you the name of your trusty steed for the day. We will help you onto your horse and give instructions on how to ride our quality and exceptional horses 🐎

The ride to the pub is approx two hours each way and we spend a good amount of time to eat a delicious meal and relax before getting back in the saddle to ride home. 

We head out along the scenic Brisbane Valley Rail Trail, where we often see koalas & other Aussie wildlife.

 As we expect all riders to be at least comfortable at a rising trot, we will have opportunities to do so. Those more experienced will have an opportunity to canter (weather permitting) if they wish.

*Please note that if our staff are concerned about your riding ability, they may ask you NOT to join the faster group. Saftey comes first!!

If you are not a seasoned rider, you might have some sore parts after a day in the saddle!

##Consider When Booking 
Rider Weight Limit: 95kg (105kg if highly experienced rider, contact us prior to booking) 
Minimum Age: 13yrs+ (can take highly experienced 11-12 yrs old, contact us prior to booking)
Skill Level: Suitable for Novice to Experienced Riders
Time in Saddle: Approx 4hrs
Group Size: 5-12 Riders
Arrive: 30 mins before the ride
Saddles: Fenders & Western
Horse Breeds: Stock & Quarter Horses

##Skill levels we ask for
Novice (Able to confidently control a horse at a rising trot 30+ hrs in the saddle) 
Intermediate (able to control a horse at walk, trot, canter outside of an arena)
Experienced (ridden all their lives, professional rider, competed, etc.)

##What to Wear: 
Long pants, closed in shoes & suggest shirt with sleeves

##What to bring 
- Water bottle & sunscreen 
- Jeans or riding pants, sleeved shirt & boots (or some smooth soled shoes) are required to ride. 
- Also bring a water bottle to take with you in the saddlebag.
- We have helmets available to use if you don't have one (all riders must wear helmets)

All riders must arrive at least 30 minutes before their scheduled ride, all customers will be fitted with a suitable helmet, fill out waivers (if not done online) and will take part in the mandatory safety briefing.

field_values.redo_desc_about: Discover seasonally available oysters, from Sydney Rock Oysters to the Akoya pearl oyster, during a guided tasting and shucking demonstration at the harvest table. Cruise the scenic Hawkesbury River to the saltwater paddocks, learn why this environment suits oyster cultivation, and taste oysters fresh from the shell. The experience combines on-water views with land-based interpretation, offering insight into local aquaculture and the connection between oysters, community and place.
field_values.redo_desc_highlights:
* Taste seasonally available oysters including Sydney Rock and Akoya pearl oysters
* Only location where you can taste the unique akoya pearl oysters
* Learn oyster shucking technique at the harvest table
* Cruise scenic Hawkesbury River and visit working oyster leases
* Insights into oyster cultivation and local marine environment
field_values.redo_desc_what_excluded: Secrets of Pearling add-on and oyster and pearl lovers experience available as separate paid options; oysters by the dozen available to purchase subject to availability.

Order of tours may vary on day.

This one-day, two-dive course provides hands-on training for confident altitude diving. Explore the unique world of altitude diving, where you’ll learn crucial skills for high-altitude environments and deepen your understanding of decompression theory.
Practice hands-on buoyancy techniques, from weight adjustments to fine-tuning breath control, under the guidance of an instructor.
In small group sessions, you’ll cover essential topics like the physiological effects of altitude, equipment adjustments, and using the Recreational Dive Planner at higher elevations.
There are no tricky currents or waves to deal with, creating a serene diving experience.
**By the end, you’ll have stronger control and ease in the water, allowing you to dive with precision and confidence.**

description: #This one-day, two-dive course provides hands-on training for confident altitude diving.

###Program Overview:
Explore the unique world of altitude diving, where you’ll learn crucial skills for high-altitude environments and deepen your understanding of decompression theory.

###Requirements: 

- Open Water certification
- Minimum age: 15

###What to Expect:

**Face-to-face learning with your Instructor:**
Practice hands-on buoyancy techniques, from weight adjustments to fine-tuning breath control, under the guidance of an instructor.

In small group sessions, you’ll cover essential topics like the physiological effects of altitude, equipment adjustments, and using the Recreational Dive Planner at higher elevations. With face-to-face theory sessions and two practical dives, you'll gain the skills for safe, precise altitude diving.

###Location:

**Crater Lakes:**
Dive at Crater Lakes National Park (Lake Barrine or Lake Eacham), where calm, elevated waters offer a perfect setting for this specialty course. There are no tricky currents or waves to deal with, creating a serene diving experience.

###What's Included:

- Pick-up/drop-off from Cairns
- All SCUBA and snorkel gear 
- In-water training
- PADI certification

###What to Bring:

- Personal snorkel/SCUBA gear (optional)
- Water, snacks, and lunch - or can be purchased at your location
- Towel, sunscreen, and hat

**By the end, you’ll have stronger control and ease in the water, allowing you to dive with precision and confidence.**

field_values.redo_desc_about:
Delve into the fascinating depths of the ocean with our distinguished underwater exploration course. Unveil a world of wonder as you embark on a captivating journey, diving to depths between 18 and 40 meters. By mastering the art of deep diving, you'll become a highly sought-after asset in the dive industry, opening up new opportunities for career advancement and recognition as a skilled and accomplished diver.
This unit describes the performance outcomes, skills, and knowledge required to plan and complete deep recreational SCUBA dives to a maximum depth of 40 meters using equipment, diving, and risk management techniques specific to deep diving.*
In small groups, our expert instructors will guide you in controlled deep dives, effective communication, and emergency protocols to enhance your deep diving skills.
Crater Lakes National Park (Lake Barrine or Lake Eacham) offer calm, current-free waters surrounded by rainforest.
There are no tricky currents or waves to deal with, creating a serene diving experience.
**By the end of this course, you’ll have the skills and confidence to explore deeper underwater sites safely and responsibly, expanding your diving experiences and capabilities.**
